Paper_Metadata.Paper_Title: Calphad-assisted design of high strength – ductility martensitic stainless-steels with reverted austenite

Process_Text.original: Samples with different compositions are produced by Edmund Buhler arc melting system AM500 with suction casting. Then the ingots are cold rolled or hot rolled to target thickness and homogenized at 1000 °C for 3 h with a water quench.
Process_Text.simplified: Arc melting → suction casting → cold/hot rolling → homogenization at 1000 °C / 3 h / water quench

Structure_Text.original: Reverted austenite forms in 10Ni4Mo at 530 °C. After 1 h at 530 °C, austenite volume fraction is 12.2% (EBSD). Austenite grains nucleate at martensite boundaries as thin film and bulky morphologies. Thin film austenite thickness < 1 μm.
Structure_Text.simplified: Martensite with NiAl-B2 precipitates and ~12% reverted austenite; austenite nucleates at martensite boundaries

Process_Text.original: Homogenized at 1000 °C for 3 h with water quench, then annealed at 580 °C for various times (15 min, 1 h, 4 h, 8 h).
Process_Text.simplified: Homogenization 1000 °C / 3 h / WQ → annealing 580 °C / various times

Structure_Text.original: Hardness increases initially then decreases with annealing time at 580 °C, indicating overaging after 15 min. Softening behavior analyzed via Orowan mechanism.
Structure_Text.simplified: Overaged condition at 580 °C; precipitation coarsening dominant after 15 min

Secondary_Phases.Note: Precipitate coarsening occurs during annealing at 580 °C

Overaging_onset.Note: Softening starts after ~15 min annealing at 580 °C

Coarsening_rate_M.Note: 8Ni has higher coarsening rate constant M than 8Ni4Mo (from linear fit of ΔH^(-3) vs time, Fig. 6b inset)

Properties.Note: Hardness values plotted in Fig. 6b; exact numerical values not given in text. Shows initial hardening (as-quenched to 15 min) then softening (overaging).

Process_Text.original: Homogenized at 1000 °C for 3 h with water quench, then annealed at 580 °C for various times (15 min, 1 h, 4 h).
Process_Text.simplified: Homogenization 1000 °C / 3 h / WQ → annealing 580 °C / various times

Structure_Text.original: No austenite formation even after 4 h of annealing at 580 °C. NiAl-B2 precipitates maintain semi-coherent interface after 4 h at 580 °C.
Structure_Text.simplified: Martensite with NiAl-B2 precipitates (semi-coherent after 4 h at 580 °C), no reverted austenite

Secondary_Phases.Note: Confirmed by TEM diffraction (Fig. 5c); diffraction pattern from sample with 4 h annealing at 580 °C

Coarsening_rate_comparison.Note: 8Ni4Mo exhibits less softening than 8Ni, confirming lower coarsening rate due to Mo addition

Properties.Note: Hardness values plotted in Fig. 6b; exact numerical values not given in text. 8Ni4Mo shows less softening than 8Ni.

Process_Text.original: Homogenized at 1000 °C for 3 h with water quench, then annealed at 580 °C for various times (15 min, 1 h, 4 h).
Process_Text.simplified: Homogenization 1000 °C / 3 h / WQ → annealing 580 °C / various times

Structure_Text.original: At 580 °C, 10Ni4Mo forms 11.4% austenite after 15 min, 18.6% after 1 hour, and 37.3% after 4 h. Austenite nucleates at martensite boundaries. Thin film austenite (thickness < 1 μm) and bulky austenite observed. Banded austenite structure along rolling normal direction due to dendritic segregation.
Structure_Text.simplified: Martensite with NiAl-B2 precipitates and increasing reverted austenite fraction with annealing time at 580 °C

Secondary_Phases.Morphology: thin film at martensite boundaries and bulky grains
Secondary_Phases.Note: Thin film austenite thickness < 1 μm. Banded structure along normal direction of rolled sheet.

Ni_segregation_variation.Note: Ni concentration varies within 8-13 at.% along cross-section with ~13 μm length scale due to dendritic segregation (SEM-EDS line scan, low-pass FFT filtered)

Mo_segregation_variation.Note: Mo concentration varies within 2-3 at.% along cross-section

Expected_eq_austenite_fraction_variation.Note: ThermoCalc-calculated equilibrium austenite fraction varies between 0.1 and 0.4 along cross-section due to segregation

Properties.Note: Hardness values plotted in Fig. 6b; exact numerical values not given in text.

Experiment_Link.Description: ECCI and synchrotron diffraction analysis of dislocation density evolution in 10Ni4Mo at 530 °C with different annealing times

Process_Text.original: Homogenized at 1000 °C for 3 h with water quench, then annealed at 530 °C for various times.
Process_Text.simplified: Homogenization 1000 °C / 3 h / WQ → annealing 530 °C / various times

Structure_Text.original: Dislocation density of martensite significantly decreases after short annealing time, then becomes negligible decrease from 1 h to 8 h, suggesting precipitate pinning effect. BSE image shows dislocation bowing characteristics suggesting pinning by precipitates.
Structure_Text.simplified: Dislocation density decreases rapidly initially then stabilizes due to precipitate pinning

Secondary_Phases.Note: Dislocation bowing characteristics observed in ECCI imaging, suggesting precipitate pinning effect

Dislocation_density_evolution.Note: Dislocation density in martensite significantly decreases after short annealing, negligible decrease from 1 h to 8 h (Fig. 11b). Precipitate pinning effect limits further dislocation annihilation.
